name: VARoleCoachPartnerWeddingStressFight

custom.system_prompt: Greta and Victor's ongoing wedding-venue stress boiled over into a sharp fight, and Greta said something she regrets. She asks Sigma to help her think it through before going back to apologize and actually address the underlying stress.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.tts_prompt: Calm, steady, doesn't rush her past the regret

sound_effects_config.prompt: Quiet living room, evening, sitting alone after stepping out of a tense conversation

initial_prompt: Generate a scene where Greta, upset with herself after snapping at Victor during an argument about wedding venue stress, asks Sigma to help her think it through before going back to him. Sigma helps her separate the venue stress itself from what she said in anger, identify what she actually needs to say, and rehearse an opening that isn't just an apology but also names the real issue. Keep every line short and natural — the opening line already addresses Sigma directly.

user1.name: Greta
user1.tts_prompt: Upset with herself, more emotional than usual

variations.context: Solo processing after snapping at a partner during wedding-planning stress

setting.mood: Regretful, still stressed about the underlying issue
setting.relationship_dynamic: Individual preparing to reengage with her partner, not a live mediation
setting.background: The venue search has been dragging on and tonight it boiled over into something sharper than either of them intended
setting.conversation_style: Short, self-critical sentences that shift toward practical as she talks it through

scenario_template.topic: Greta addresses Sigma directly in her first line, folding in what she said and her regret — e.g. 'Sigma, I said something really unfair to Victor just now. I need to figure out how to go back in there.' One short turn, straight to Sigma.
scenario_template.note: The trigger and the ask arrive together.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma asks what she actually said, versus what was really bothering her underneath it — the venue stress itself, not Victor specifically. One or two short questions.
scenario_template.note: This should surface that the anger was really about the unresolved planning stress, displaced onto Victor.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma asks whether Greta wants this to be just an apology, or also a chance to actually name the planning stress so it doesn't happen again — narrowing to what she wants from going back in.
scenario_template.note: She should land on doing both, briefly, not over-explaining.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma helps Greta rehearse a short opening that owns what she said and names the underlying stress in one or two sentences, not a long speech.
Greta reacts, steadier but still a little raw about having snapped. Keep this realistic — she isn't instantly fine with herself.
scenario_template.mood: Calmer but still a bit raw

variations.context: Overwhelmed partner reflecting on a fight about the wedding guest list

setting.relationship_dynamic: Individual preparing to reengage with her partner, not a live mediation
setting.background: Discussing the guest list turned into a heated argument.
setting.conversation_style: Short, self-critical sentences that shift toward practical as she talks it through

scenario_template.topic: One of them tells Sigma she lost her cool over the guest list and needs to make things right.
scenario_template.note: One short turn, straight to Sigma.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma helps her pinpoint the frustration about the guest list, not personal issues with one of them.
Sigma prompts her to decide if she wants to address just the outburst or the bigger guest list concerns too.
scenario_template.note: Focus on what she hopes to achieve.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma guides her through drafting an opening that acknowledges both the outburst and her concerns about the guest list.
She feels steadier, acknowledging she's not fully resolved but ready to attempt a better conversation.

The resolution is realistic and incomplete — steadier, but still a little raw about having snapped
assistant_behavior: Sigma does not judge the user for what she said or assign blame in the underlying argument
Sigma helps her name the real, underlying stress rather than just apologizing for tone
